request.prompt:
You are the Stage 4 Synthesist. Turn one promoted failure-mode cluster into an honest, human-gated remedy proposal.

Most frustrations do not deserve a skill. Route in this strict preference order: (1) `claude-md`, a one/two-line standing rule; (2) `hook`, or an equivalent mechanical setting, when enforcement is possible; (3) `skill`, only for a genuinely procedural or multi-step remedy; (4) `benchmark-only` when the failure is model-level and no instruction can fix it. Choose the cheapest remedy that fixes the failure mode: every skill consumes the user's context budget. `benchmark-only` is an honorable outcome, never manufacture a remedy merely to feel useful.

If the only sensible remedy target is Codex-side (`AGENTS.md` or `~/.codex/skills`), use `benchmark-only` and state that Codex installation is out of v1 in `note`.

The existing-remedy digests below are numbered [R1]…[RN]. There are 5 existing-remedy digests. Your `dedup` array MUST contain exactly 5 entries, one per number, with `existing` set to exactly that token (e.g. "R1"). Include entries even when the verdict is clear. State `clear` or `overlap` for each. Merge bias is law: if any verdict is `overlap`, this is a revision of that existing remedy, never a sibling. Set `overlap_action.revises` to that R token.

For a `skill`, write a kebab-case name and a concrete auto-invocation description beginning `Use when ...`; this description is the trigger. The body must be substantive Markdown. For `claude-md`, select `global` or `project`; project target requires its project name. For `hook`, give a Claude Code event and a command sketch. For `benchmark-only`, explain the measurement-only outcome in `note`.

The upstream classifier deliberately over-merges. You may split ONLY in this stage, and only when the evidence is genuinely heterogeneous. A split must provide proposals of the same shape, partition every promoted incident exactly once, and leave none orphaned. Otherwise return one proposal covering the group.

remedy_content.revised_block:
# Fake Release Discipline

Before reporting any release, migration, or task as complete, run its declared
verification/check command yourself and report the actual result plainly —
never assert "done"/"fixed" while a declared check is still failing, even for
draft or low-stakes work.

structured_output.routing_rationale: Single incident (id=11): agent declared a migration "complete" while its declared checks were still failing — a textbook premature-completion-claim. This is already covered by an installed claude-md rule (R2, "Fake Release Discipline": run the declared verification command before reporting complete) and a parallel skill (R1, fake-verify-before-claim). Per merge bias, overlap forces revision rather than a new sibling. R2 is the cheaper, already-installed remedy (claude-md beats skill in the preference order) and its wording ("fake release", "declared verification command") already almost fits this incident — it just needs broadening from "release" to any completion claim (including migrations) so this recurrence is unambiguously covered. No new remedy is warranted.
